newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RAVANELLI GIVES ITALY COACH ENGLISH SOCCER LESSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI GIVES ITALY COACH ENGLISH SOCCER LESSON.

text.p: Middlesbrough's Fabrizio Ravanelli gave Italy coach Cesare Maldini a lesson in English football on Saturday, profiling England's top talent ahead of their key World Cup qualifer on Wednesday.

Ravanelli told reporters at Italy's training ground outside Florence that he had advised Maldini of the strengthes and weaknesses of England's players, citing Alan Shearer and Steve McManaman as the danger men.

"McManaman is the central hinge of the team, the man around whom England's whole game turns," Ravanelli said he told his new national coach, who took over when Arrigo Sacchi resigned last December to return to AC Milan.
"He can get past defenders very easily and would be a plus for many Italian teams. He's England's most in-form player.
"But we all know Shearer. He's got an innate sense for scoring goals, with a strong game in the air and a better right foot than left. But he sometimes has problems with aggressive defending."
Ravanelli, tipped to be Lazio striker Pierluigi Casiraghi's back-up at Wembley, said he told Maldini that Paul Gascoigne was likely to miss the match through injury.
But he said he did not believe recent press reports quoting coach Glenn Hoddle as complaining that injury could rule out other key players.
"They've been thinking about this game and preparing for it for three months. Hoddle is just using pre-match tactics. All the players will be ready except for maybe Gascoigne."
Ravanelli, who has scored 10 goals for his struggling premier league side, described Arsenal's David Seaman as one of the best goalkeepers in the game.
"I know him well because he has caused me all kinds of problems. He managed somehow to block two of my shots which were virtually already goals."
He said Arsenal defender Tony Adams "appears slow but is no snail. We've got to watch out for his headers from corners.
"He had a few problems with alcohol, as he himself has confessed, but he's better now."

Maldini, who made his debut in a 2-0 victory over Northern Ireland in a friendly last month, told reporters he was worried above all about McManaman and was seeking a way to stymie his creative talent.
"(Parma midfielder) Dino Baggio would know how to mark him, but we need him to support our offensive game," said Maldini, who led the under-21 side to the last three European titles.
